notes:
Identity verified from canonical full article: title Phantom Pains: The Effect of Police Killings of Black Americans on Black British Attitudes; author Ayobami Laniyonu; DOI 10.1017/S0007123421000557; British Journal of Political Science (2022), 52, 1651–1667. First published online 17 December 2021, consistent with the reference’s 2021 date. This is the primary research article, with methods, results, tables and references, not an abstract or secondary report. No PDF was supplied. The outcome and Black Londoner sample are identified by the article title, outcome labels and explicit Black Londoners table headings. The supplied p. 1663 locator contains both Table 2 (ITT regression discontinuity estimator without covariates) and Table 3 (ITT regression discontinuity estimator with controls), and does not identify which specification is intended. Table 2 prints −3.54 (same-row p = 0.01); Table 3 prints −3.42 (same-row p = 0.02). Both are candidates only. The printed metric is a regression discontinuity estimator on the rescaled outcome, not an explicitly standardized beta. No metric conversion or specification selection was made. Metric evidence, p. 1659: For interpretability, this outcome, along with all other
index measures described later, were rescaled so that neutral response values (“fair”) equal 0,
maximum positive values (“excellent”) equal 5 and maximum negative values (“very poor”)
equal −5. Only es_value_o is assigned; N, p and reported_success are placeholders. Same-row p values above are candidate context, not extracted p fields.
